title: The Right Edge of the Zero Set of the Fibonacci Zeta Function
summary: Let $F_1=F_2=1$, $F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_n$, and define the Fibonacci zeta function by $$ Z_F(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}F_n^{-s},\qquad \operatorname{Re}s>0. $$ We determine the exact right edge of the closure of the real parts of its zeros in the half-plane of absolute convergence. If $σ_F$ is the unique solution of $$ Z_F(σ_F)=4+2\,144^{-σ_F}, $$ then $$ σ_F=0.743163398726901648\ldots, $$ $Z_F(s)\neq0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\geσ_F$, while $$ \overline{\{\operatorname{Re}ρ:Z_F(ρ)=0,\ \operatorname{Re}ρ>0\}}=[0,σ_F]. $$ The edge is sharp in an almost-periodic sense: zeros occur with relatively dense…
